accessibility-person.context: A person with outstretched arms inside a circle, the universal access symbol. Used for accessibility settings and menus, website accessibility statements, inclusive design pages and accessible services.

audio-description.context: The letters AD with sound waves beside them. Marks audio-described films and TV, video player options, accessible theatre performances and museum audio guides.

blind-cane.context: A person walking with a long white cane. Used for blind and low-vision services, accessible routes and signage, accessibility settings and mobility training.

braille.context: A card with raised braille dots. Braille signage and documents, tactile reading, accessible packaging and services for blind readers use it.

cognitive.context: A head in profile with a spiral inside, for cognitive accessibility. Used for learning and memory support, neurodiversity resources, dementia-friendly services and focus or simplify settings.

easy-read.context: A page of small pictures next to short lines of text. Found on easy read versions of documents, plain language summaries, learning disability resources and simplified content toggles.

hearing-loop.context: An ear with the letter T, the sign for a hearing loop. Shown at counters, venues and ticket desks where an induction loop is fitted, and in accessibility guides.

low-vision.context: An eye with a partly broken outline, for low vision. Used for low-vision settings, high contrast and large text modes, sight loss services and accessibility menus.

mobility-aid.context: A wheeled walking frame, also called a rollator. Used for mobility equipment shops, elderly and home care services, step-free access notes and rehab or physiotherapy.

service-dog.context: A guide dog wearing a harness with a handle. Common on signs welcoming assistance dogs, blind and low-vision services, venue access policies and pet rules.

sign-language.context: A hand in the middle of signing, with motion marks. Used for sign language interpretation, signed video content, deaf services and accessibility options at events and in media.
